The '''Rakata Prime system''' lay in the [[Unknown Regions]] and contained the [[planet]] [[Rakata Prime]], the [[homeworld]] of the [[Rakatan]] [[species]]. Traveling off-world, they eventually established the [[Infinite Empire]] but supposedly ultimately went extinct. At some point between [[34 ABY]] and [[35 ABY]], a [[Rakata Prime refueling station|refueling station]] [[orbit]]ed the planet, and the facility was visited by the [[chef]] [[Strono Tuggs]].

==Description==
The Rakata Prime system was located in the [[Unknown Regions]] in grid square G-11 of the [[Standard Galactic Grid]].<ref name="Appendix" /> It contained the terrestrial<ref name="SWR">{{Resistance|Rendezvous Point (episode)}}</ref> [[planet]]<ref name="BMF 47">{{BuildFalconCite|47|Secrets of Spaceflight}}</ref> [[Rakata Prime]]. Although the cosmic bramble of [[Hyperspace anomaly|hyperspace anomalies]] known as the [[Galactic Barrier]] generally hindered the [[Scout|exploration]] of the Unknown Regions from [[the galaxy]]'s more central areas, Rakata Prime was among the few navigable worlds that were discovered by rare exploratory missions, and the planet could subsequently be reached by cautiously stepped [[hyperspace]] jumps.<ref name="TROS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

==History==
Rakata Prime was [[Homeworld|home]] to an [[Amphibian|amphibious]] [[species]]<ref name="BMF 47" /> known as the [[Rakatan]]s, who reputedly invented hyperspace travel.<ref name="TUC" /> They ventured off-world,<ref name="100 Objects">''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]''</ref> establishing the [[Infinite Empire]]<ref name="NoP">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref> before supposedly going extinct.<ref name="BMF 47" /> The planet itself was still known in the wider [[galaxy]]<ref name="Hunters">''[[Hunters: Battle for the Arena]]''</ref> by some point no earlier than [[9 ABY]].<ref name="Hunters date">The events of ''[[Hunters: Battle for the Arena]]'' take place after [[Aran Tal]] joined the [[Hunters of the Outer Rim]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[9 ABY]].</ref>

By [[33 ABY]],<ref name="SWA date">''[[Star Wars Adventures, Volume 1: Heroes of the Galaxy]]'' establishes that [[Tryki]] was arrested near [[Rakata Prime]] before the [[kidnapping of Unkar Plutt]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[33 ABY]].</ref> the [[Zabrak]] [[pirate]] [[Tryki]] was arrested for attempting to board a [[First Order]] [[cruiser]] near Rakata Prime.<ref name="SWA">''[[Star Wars Adventures, Volume 1: Heroes of the Galaxy]]''</ref> The [[human]] [[Resistance pilot]] [[Venisa Doza]] and her [[R-series|astromech droid]], [[Torch]], also visited the planet<ref name="SWR" /> at one point by [[34 ABY]].<ref name="SWT">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> By sometime between that [[Standard year|year]] and [[35 ABY]],<ref name="TUC date">{{UltimateCookbookDate}}</ref> a [[Rakata Prime refueling station|refueling station]] [[orbit]]ed Rakata Prime, and the facility was visited by the [[Artiodac]] [[chef]] [[Strono Tuggs]].<ref name="TUC" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Unkwld_space.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Rakata Prime system in the ''Star Wars'' Legends continuity]]
The Rakata Prime [[Star system|system]] was first mentioned in the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] on a [[map]] of the galaxy<ref name="Empire Magazine">{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/news/exclusive-empire-reveals-new-star-wars-planets|text=Exclusive: Empire reveals names of new Star Wars planets|author=De Semlyen, Phil|date=2015-11-26|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|archivedate=20160507021312}}</ref> created for ''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]'',<ref name="Hidalgo tweet">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/669926716974870528|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2015-11-26|quote=WARNING, INCOMING PLUG: That galaxy map was generated for the TFA Visual Dictionary, btw. PLUG COMPLETE.|nolive=1}}</ref> a reference book written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and published on [[December 18]], [[2015]].<ref name="DK">{{DK|url=us/book/9781465438164-star-wars-the-force-awakens-the-visual-dictionary|text=Star Wars: The Force Awakens The Visual Dictionary}}</ref> The map was initially revealed prior to the book's release through an article by [[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']] magazine on [[November 26]] of the same year.<ref name="Empire Magazine" /> The [[star]] system was then identified by name in "[[Star Systems of the Galaxy]]," an appendix published with the [[Star Wars Galaxy Map|''Star Wars'' Galaxy Map]] on [[StarWars.com]]<ref name="Appendix" /> on [[June 24]], 2025. Both works were authored by [[Jason Fry]].<ref name="Substack">{{Substack|subdomain=jasonfry|url=p/about-that-new-star-wars-galaxy-map|text=About That New Star Wars Galaxy Map…|name=[[Jason Fry]]|username=jasonfry|date=2025-06-24}}</ref>

The [[Lehon system|star system]] was originally introduced in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it first appeared as the "Star Forge system" in<ref name="KotOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> the [[July 15]], [[2003]]<ref name="Anniversary">{{SW|url=news/kotor-galaxy-of-heroes|text=BioWare and Capital Games on Bringing ''KotOR'' Fan Favorites into ''Galaxy of Heroes''|nolive=1}}</ref> [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''. A screenshot from the game showing the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="KotOR" /> [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and therefore its [[Star system/Legends|system]], was featured on StarWars.com on [[May 2]], 2003.<ref name="SWcom">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/news20030502.html|text=KOTOR coming to PC}}</ref> The [[2006]] novel ''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'', written by [[Drew Karpyshyn]] as the first entry in the ''[[Star Wars: Darth Bane Trilogy]]'', first identified the system as the "Lehon system,"<ref name="PoD">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> while the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and Jason Fry provided the alternative identification "Rakata Prime system."<ref name="TEA" />
